# Lacuna v0.6.0

Lacuna `v0.6.0` completes the optional-integration milestone. External data, backtest artifacts,
estimator cross-validation, and third-party code now cross explicit, evidenced boundaries without
expanding the core runtime dependency surface.

## Highlights

- DuckDB result ingestion through an Arrow record-batch stream without pandas or Lacuna-generated
  SQL, including explicit legacy-reader evidence.
- A dependency-free scikit-learn cross-validation bridge over frozen walk-forward, purged, or CPCV
  folds, with original Lacuna interval evidence retained.
- Immutable vendor schemas declaring availability, revisions, timezones, price adjustment, and
  identifier semantics.
- Generic return, trade, and position adapters that require gross/net, compounding, timing, delay,
  price, cost, borrow, calendar, session, missing-instrument, and delisting assumptions.
- Metadata-only Python entry-point discovery, conflict-safe selection, and explicit trusted-code
  activation with protocol-major and capability negotiation.
- A separately packaged `lacuna-options` `0.1.0` distribution for validated option chains, carry
  forwards, log-forward moneyness, absolute-delta buckets, and empirical IV residuals.
- Independent frozen core `0.6.x` and options `0.1.x` export/signature contracts; real DuckDB and
  scikit-learn integration tests; options property/adversarial tests; and clean joint-wheel smoke.

## Trust and methodology boundaries

Plugin discovery does not import target modules. Activation is a deliberate in-process trust
decision and is not a sandbox. Vendor and backtest adapters translate declared artifacts; they do
not certify point-in-time truth, run a backtest, or invent methodology. The DuckDB adapter accepts an
already executed trusted result and never constructs SQL.

The initial options extension does not claim a universal IV solver, Greeks model, SVI calibration,
arbitrage repair, or delta-hedged attribution. Those require explicit model, exercise, settlement,
curve, dividend, calendar, and numerical contracts.

## Compatibility and distribution

The core change is additive over every published `0.1.x` through `0.5.x` contract. The extension has
its own `0.1.x` version and supports `lacuna>=0.5,<0.7`; publishing both in one GitHub Release does
not couple their future version numbers.

This release is distributed through GitHub because the `lacuna` name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated
project. The release contains four target-smoke-tested CPython 3.11 stable-ABI core wheels, one
universal options wheel, both source distributions, `SHA256SUMS`, and GitHub provenance for every
distribution.

The full implementation record is in the
[changelog](https://github.com/eyenoticeall/Lacuna/blob/v0.6.0/CHANGELOG.md). Exact adapter, plugin,
trust, materialization, and compatibility contracts are in the
[adapter/plugin guide](https://github.com/eyenoticeall/Lacuna/blob/v0.6.0/docs/subsystems/adapters-execution-plugins.md)
and the
[options extension guide](https://github.com/eyenoticeall/Lacuna/blob/v0.6.0/docs/subsystems/options-extension.md).
